confirmed_map_writers.writes: STL `_Tree<>::lower_bound` style helper. Walks from header[1] via piVar[0]/[2] left/right pointers comparing piVar[3] (the key) against *param_3. If exact match found, returns iter with byte[2]=0 (existing). Otherwise calls FUN_004de610 to insert and returns iter with byte[2]=1 (newly inserted).

confirmed_map_writers.name: ZoneActorMap_RedBlackTreeInsert_FUN_004de610
confirmed_map_writers.writes: Low-level STL insert. Allocates a new node via FUN_004ddf20 (caller-provided header, key, value). Increments *(map+8) (the size). Links the new node into the tree (header[1]/leftmost or via parent[0]/[2] left/right slots). Then runs the standard red-black-tree rebalance loop (the cVar1 != 0 loop reading parent.color at +0x14, switching between FUN_006ceef0 and FUN_00b9f240 = the LEFT_ROTATE and RIGHT_ROTATE functions). Finally sets header[1].color = 1 (black-root invariant).
confirmed_map_writers.implication: The actual map mutation primitive. Writes happen at: new_node[1] = parent, new_node[2]/[0] = sentinels (set by FUN_004ddf20), color flags via the rebalance loop, header pointers (+0/+4/+8 of header) when leftmost/rightmost change. Storage layout: each node has +0=left, +4=parent, +8=right, +0xc=key (the actor id), +0x10=value (actor pointer), +0x14=color byte, +0x15=is_nil flag.

resolution_explanation: The actor-vtable9-bulk pass left open: 'where does the Actor cluster processing actually happen for 0xCC..0xE5 if not in vftable[9] of any cataloged actor class?' This directly identifies the actor type stored in the zone+0x17804 map: Application::Main::RaptureElement. Its full vftable[0..15] has been dumped. Slot 9 = FUN_0091F6F0 is a 32-byte 'set context/parent' hook that calls FUN_0091F620 and FUN_00571BB0(this, 0) - NOT a packet handler. So the empirical refutation from the actor-vtable9-bulk pass EXTENDS to RaptureElement as well: the base class slot 9 is not an opcode dispatcher. HOWEVER: this reveals the RaptureElement class hierarchy is INVISIBLE to the actor-vtable9-bulk pass's RTTI scan because that scan searched for class names containing 'Actor' (e.g. SceneObject::Actor, ::Actor descendants). RaptureElement is the engine's PARALLEL actor-like hierarchy living under Application::Main::Element rather than Application::Scene::Actor. The 22 derived classes (the 22 callers of FUN_004dab50) likely override slot 9 differently. So the actor-vtable9-bulk pass's negative result for the SQEX SceneObject side is correct, but a complementary FUN_004D9910 callers-map pass should drill the 22 RaptureElement subclasses' slot 9 implementations - that's where the actual Actor cluster processing logic likely lives. This therefore PARTIALLY RESOLVES the open question from the actor-vtable9-bulk pass: it identifies the right class hierarchy to investigate, but base-class slot 9 still shows no opcode dispatch. The 22 derived subclasses remain unenumerated.

key_findings.title: The zone actor map stores Application::Main::RaptureElement*, not SQEX SceneObject::Actor*
key_findings.detail: The actor-vtable9-bulk pass exhaustively searched the SceneObject::Actor RTTI hierarchy (95 classes) for an opcode-dispatching vftable[9] and found none. This reveals this is because the actor type in the zone map is a DIFFERENT class hierarchy: Application::Main::RaptureElement, rooted at vftable 0x00F91014. This is the engine's element-management hierarchy (Application::Main namespace) rather than the scene-graph (Application::Scene::Actor namespace). Direct RTTI evidence comes from FUN_004daf00's dynamic_cast calls against both Application::Main::RaptureElement::RTTI_Type_Descriptor and Application::Main::Element::RelativeElement::RTTI_Type_Descriptor. The 22 derived subclasses (the 22 callers of the base ctor FUN_004dab50) span 0x55XXXX/0x66XXXX/0x68XXXX VA ranges, suggesting one per major game subsystem.
key_findings.implication: The actor-vtable9-bulk pass's 'no actor class has a real slot 9' finding is correct but framed against the wrong hierarchy. The real question of where the Actor cluster opcodes are processed shifts to: 'do any of the 22 RaptureElement subclasses override slot 9 with a real opcode dispatcher?' FUN_004D9910 callers-map pass candidate work.

key_findings.title: Exactly one insertion path: FUN_004dab50 (RaptureElement::ctor) -> FUN_004da9a0 -> FUN_004de940 -> FUN_004de610 -> FUN_004ddf20
key_findings.detail: There is no alternative insertion path. Every actor that enters the zone map goes through the RaptureElement ctor. FUN_004da9a0 is the single caller-of-FUN_004de940 reachable from the actor-creation chain; FUN_004de940 is the single caller of FUN_004de610. No other function in the binary writes new nodes to the zone+0x17804 tree.
key_findings.implication: The actor map's contents are exactly the live set of RaptureElement instances. Any 'AddActor' opcode (0xCA per BCS-Y-0525) eventually triggers a derived ctor which calls FUN_004dab50; the actor is inserted with key=class_id at value=this. The lookup BCS-Y-0534 FUN_004d9910 then returns this RaptureElement* on subsequent opcodes.

key_findings.title: Three erasure paths exist, gated by zone+0x17820 'is_being_destroyed' flag and zone teardown
key_findings.detail: Single-element erase: FUN_004dac20 (BCS-Y-0543) - either hard-erase (FUN_004de280) or soft-erase (*(iter+0x10)=0). Range erase: FUN_004de540 / FUN_004de900 / FUN_004dea70 - for zone-wide teardown. The soft-erase path leaves the map node IN the tree with a null value - which means lookups via FUN_004d9910 (BCS-Y-0534) can return 0 (the function explicitly checks `if (local_4 == *(int *)(local_8 + 4)) FUN_009d22b4()` and returns *(local_4 + 0x10) which would be 0 for soft-deleted nodes). FUN_004d9ca0 (BCS-Y-0540's sibling, the next-free-id scanner) explicitly walks the tree checking for *(iter+0x10)==0 to find recyclable slots.
key_findings.implication: Map nodes can outlive the actors they pointed to. Slot 9 dispatch via the BCS-Y-0527 generic fallthrough COULD hit a soft-deleted node and would then call vftable[9] on a null pointer - but the actual code does `actor = FUN_004d9910(packet_id); if (actor) actor->vftable[9](zone_state)` (per actor_cluster_dispatch_model.json line 759, wrapped in an if-check), so the null case is gracefully skipped.

key_findings.title: FUN_004d9980 (case-2 sibling) is a SINGLETON slot maintenance helper, not a map writer
key_findings.detail: Prior evidence hinted FUN_004d9980 was 'a sibling of FUN_004d90c0'. This confirms it does NOT write to the map - it maintains the zone+0x17838/+0x1783c/+0x17840 'active actor' singleton slots. The previous-active-actor pointer goes to +0x17840, the new-active-id to +0x1783c, and the new-active-actor-pointer to +0x17838 (computed via FUN_004d9910 lookup). Sentinel id 0xc0000000 clears all three slots.
key_findings.implication: These three singleton slots are the 'currently selected/active actor' state that BCS-Y-0531's case-2 dispatch path operates on, NOT the map itself. The map and the singleton are independent state - the map holds all actors, the singletons hold the active one.

key_findings.title: The actor map's STL tree uses a 0x18-byte node, NOT the 0x24-byte std::map<int,int>::node_type the actor-factory-drill pass implicitly assumed
key_findings.detail: FUN_004de280 (erase) and FUN_004de610 (insert) both call FUN_0044d350 (the deallocator) with constants (0x18, 0x20) which match std::map<dword,dword>::value_type node size. Node layout: +0x00 left, +0x04 parent, +0x08 right, +0x0c key, +0x10 value, +0x14 color, +0x15 is_nil. This is `std::map<uint32_t,RaptureElement*>::value_type` (key+value 8 bytes, plus 16 bytes of tree metadata = 0x18 = 24 bytes).
key_findings.implication: Worth promoting to a BCS-S struct entry. Future map-walker code in subsequent phases can reference this layout directly.

open_questions.q: Do any of the 22 RaptureElement-derived subclasses override slot 9 (offset 0x24) with a real opcode dispatcher?
open_questions.approach: FUN_004D9910 callers-map pass candidate work. Enumerate the 22 callers of FUN_004dab50, for each identify the derived class vftable (probably set by the caller itself BEFORE calling the base ctor), then bulk-dump slot 9 across all 22 vftables via DumpVtableSlots.java. Compare against the base FUN_0091F6F0 - any deviation is a candidate handler. Test for switch-on-opcode patterns or 0xCC..0xE5 immediate comparisons in the deviating implementations.

open_questions.q: Is RTTI for Application::Main::RaptureElement and its 22 derived subtypes actually present in the binary, or is it stripped?
open_questions.approach: FUN_004daf00's dynamic_cast usage proves RTTI exists for at least RaptureElement and RelativeElement. The FUN_004D9910 callers-map pass could grep for 'Application::Main::*::RTTI_Type_Descriptor' to enumerate. If all 22 are RTTI-named, that step becomes mechanical.
This inferred its role from FUN_004de610 usage but did not decompile. One-shot decomp would confirm the node's actor-pointer goes to +0x10 of the allocated block and verify the 0x18-byte size.

new_ghidra_scripts.purpose: Scans every instruction for displacement-scalar references matching IMPLEMENTATION_OFFSET_QUERY (comma-separated hex offsets), with a minimum threshold BAHAMUT_MIN_OFFSET to filter out stack-locals. Reports VA + containing-function + instruction text per hit. This validated this approach is too restrictive for compiler-generated [reg+offset] addressing where the offset appears in a SIB byte rather than a separate scalar operand. Future phases may need to extend the script to also walk PCodeOp.LOAD/STORE addresses to catch these cases.
